text: Think from first principles, not by analogy.
Invert, always invert.
Carry a notebook everywhere. Write everything down.
Develop a latticework of mental models across many disciplines.
Sit with a problem long enough. Deep focus is a superpower.
Question every assumption, especially popular ones.
Read broadly and deeply, every day for life.
Update your beliefs when evidence changes. Never be the prisoner of your old conclusions.
Spend time thinking about thinking — your metacognition is your operating system.
Avoid the news. Study history instead.
Do the thing you're working on at the highest quality possible, always.
Work harder and longer than anyone else expects.
Embrace deep practice: isolate the hardest part and repeat it deliberately.
Master the fundamentals so completely they become instinct.
Finish what you start. Completion is rare and therefore valuable.
Show up every single day, especially when you don't want to.
Make enemies of distraction and comfort.
Seek the hardest challenges, not the easiest wins.
Say no to almost everything so you can say yes fully to the few things that matter.
Do your most important work when your mental energy is at its peak.
Know your enemy and yourself before every battle.
Move fast, hit where there is no defense, never where they are strongest.
Play long games with long-term people.
Preserve optionality. Never paint yourself into a corner.
Build systems, not goals.
Control the narrative. Whoever frames the story controls the outcome.
Use your opponent's strength against them.
source_figure: Judo principle, Sun Tzu, Genghis Khan

text: Concentrate your forces. Diluted effort produces diluted results.
Choose your battles. Not every fight is worth winning.
Spend less than you earn. Always. No exceptions.
Invest early and let compounding do the work.
Never lose money. Rule two: never forget rule one.
Understand what you own and why. Never invest in what you don't understand.
Create multiple streams of income. One source is a single point of failure.
Your network is your net worth. Invest in relationships obsessively.
Build assets that work while you sleep.
Pay yourself first. Automate savings before you have a chance to spend.
source_figure: Franklin, George Clason (The Richest Man in Babylon)

text: Know the difference between assets and liabilities — and only buy assets.
source_figure: Robert Kiyosaki's synthesis of Carnegie, Rockefeller

text: Give significantly. Generosity is both ethical and strategically wise.
Move your body every single day. Motion is medicine.
Sleep is performance. Protect it as a non-negotiable.
Eat to fuel performance, not for pleasure as a primary driver.
Train for both strength and endurance.
Avoid substances that dull the mind. Guard your cognitive clarity above all.
Cold exposure and physical hardship voluntarily sought toughens the mind.
Manage stress actively — it is the silent destroyer of health and performance.
Do what you say you will do. Integrity is the foundation of everything.
Take full ownership of your life. Stop blaming external circumstances.
Be brutally honest with yourself first, diplomatic with others.
Cultivate humility. The smarter you get, the more you know you don't know.
Never complain. Never explain. Deliver results and let your work speak.
Be kind. Not naive — kind. There is a difference.
Develop thick skin. Criticism is the price of doing anything significant.
Practice courage daily in small things to build it for large ones.
Forgive quickly — not for others, but for yourself.
